Target H-SOM (only source text; you do not have a reference answer):
Physical trauma reactions can persist after the danger has passed, even when you know you're safe. With complex or developmental trauma, direct work on the deepest memory can be overwhelming, so a gradual approach may be enough: Buddhist nun Pema Chodron calls it a “feather touch,” and Peter Levine, the founder of Somatic Experiencing, calls gentle work around the edges “pendulation.” The same limit appears in inner-child therapy: you can know what the younger part needs yet enter the child-state so fully that too little adult perspective remains to provide it.

Here are two successful transformations from previous work. Study HOW their thoughts move, not their vocabulary. Do not copy exact phrases, examples or subject matter into your answer.

Example 1 — source:
Maybe you’ve been trying to comfort your little one for weeks, and the words are all there, but the loving grown-up behind them isn’t, not yet. Some people at that point might try saying sweeter and sweeter things, and then upon that not working, perhaps just “throw the baby out with the bathwater,” and decide reparenting is useless. I’d borrow that grown-up first. Then try again, and see if your little one can tell the difference.
Example 1 — meaning-checked, Pangram-Human realization:
Maybe you've been trying to offer your little one comfort for weeks, and the words are all there, but the loving grown-up behind them isn't there yet. Some people keep trying sweeter and sweeter things, then throw the baby out with the bathwater when that doesn't help and decide reparenting is useless. I'd borrow that grown-up first, try again, and see if your little one can tell the difference.

Example 2 — source:
The harm happened, and the boundary still matters. The person is still accountable, and forgiveness may come later on its own.
Example 2 — owner-endorsed, Pangram-Human realization:
They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them.

The first expresses an actual sequence (sweetened words, then abandonment) instead of a cautious maze of qualifications. The second lets actual people and consequences do the work of several balanced propositions. These are observations, not a phrase bank. They don't give permission to change meaning.

Target H-CHICKEN (only source text; you do not have a reference answer):
But here’s the chicken-and-egg problem. What if you’re so far inside the child-state that you can’t become the adult? This is much easier when you can already reach one of those adult roles. Without that, you can sit there trying to say all the loving things while the old critic, numbness, panic, or urge to get away is running the whole thing.
